prompt: I need a vertical unboxing of my Hollyland headset kit, 40 seconds to a minute, that goes from the sealed box, through the case and what's in it, to me wearing one. Put an AI voice-over under the whole thing, start to finish, in a relaxed, friendly, conversational voice, like one shooter talking to another, reading exactly: 'This is the Hollyland Solid Comm C1 Pro. Hollyland was kind enough to send this out for me to test. I have the 4S variation meaning that I have one master headset and three slave headsets. I found that when I was shooting weddings, it was hard to communicate with my team. Texting and phone calls was not the answer. Most of the time my team would either miss my call or never see my texts. This is where the Hollyland Solid Comm C1 Pro comes handy. It allows me to communicate with my team with ease. Ever wonder who your second shooter is filming during the ceremony? Just tilt your microphone and ask. Stressed about your battery and don't have an extra on hand? Just ask your second shooter. Let Hollyland help your team communicate more clearly on your next production.' Open on one box landing, flat and centred on the desk with no nudging, then my finger tapping the white label while it's still readable, not my palm flat over it. Skip the tape being cut entirely. When the case opens, show the Hollyland Ecosystem brochure coming out on top, just a glimpse, no flipping through pages. When I'm wearing the headset, use one clean flip of the boom mic down where my hand stays off my face, punch in close on the mic as it comes down, and land 'Just tilt your microphone and ask' on it. End on the two headsets held side by side with the 'M' and '1' labels readable as the last line plays. Leave out me swapping the ear pad on the headset and the rummaging and repacking with my arms in the case, and no on-screen text.
concept: A wedding videographer unboxes their Hollyland Solid Comm C1 Pro headset kit while explaining how it keeps a shoot team talking, opening on the sealed box landing on the desk and ending on two headsets side by side.

Set it over the pegboard, clear of the top and right edges, on that shot only; no other text. Add a calm, friendly tutorial-style AI voice-over from start to end, each line over its step, reading exactly: 'We spend thousands of dollars on camera gear, but when was the last time you actually gave yours a proper cleaning? Use a lens wipe to clean the front element. Then use an air blower to clean the rear element. Make sure the lens is facing downwards so any dust or debris will fall out of the lens. Now do the same with your camera sensor. You want to make sure to face your sensor downwards to dislodge any dust or debris and have it fall out of the sensor area. Now that you've cleaned the inside of the camera, it's time to clean the outside. Apply a small amount of isopropyl alcohol to a q-tip to clean all the nooks and crannies of your camera. The last step is to store your clean camera and lens in an area where dust won't settle. And that's it!' Show the wipe packet torn open over the lens and the wipe pulled out, the rocket blower on the back of the lens, the bare sensor held square and still before the blower comes in, the body held sensor-down with the blower puffing up from underneath, and the swab wetted at the bottle before it goes over the dials and buttons. End on the slow two-handed put-away into the foam drawer, sharp and settling without a bump, with the drawer shutting; never show the camera coming back out. Show each step once and cut false starts, abandoned takes, caps coming off, me mopping up spilled alcohol, any cloth wiping and the camera half out of frame in a corner.
